item.title: Young finishes sixth in Commonwealth Games 50m Freestyle Final
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 27/07/2026 Team Fiji swimmer David Tolu Young produced a stellar performance in the men's 50 metres freestyle final, finishing sixth with a time of 22.18 seconds at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 27/07/2026

Team Fiji swimmer David Tolu Young produced a stellar performance in the men's 50 metres freestyle final, finishing sixth with a time of 22.18 seconds at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games.

The 21-year-old created history by becoming the first Fijian swimmer to reach a Commonwealth Games final.

Australia's Cameron McEvoy, Flynn Southam and Jamie Jack finished first, second and third respectively.

Young will compete in tonight's men's 100 metres freestyle heats, which begin at 10.09pm.

Other Team Fiji swimmers competing in the men's 100 metres freestyle heats are Hansel McCaig and Reuben Taylor.

18-year-old Kelera Mudunasoko will compete in the women's 50 metres breaststroke heats at 10.34pm.

Meanwhile, Anahira McCutcheon finished sixth in the women's 100 metres freestyle semi-finals with a time of 55.80 seconds, while Samuel Yalimaiwai finished eighth in the men's 50 metres breaststroke semi-finals.

A journey shaped by resilience, compassion and a commitment to serving others takes centre stage on this week's fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono, as Minister for Women, Children and Social Protection Sashi Kiran shares the experiences that have defined her life.

Kiran reflects on the lessons that shaped her values, and she opens up about issues close to her heart, including violence against women and children, drugs, HIV, peacebuilding, and the importance of creating opportunities for vulnerable communities.

item.title: Doctor internship graduates to be employed by next month
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 27/07/2026 Minister for Health, Doctor Ratu Atonio Lalabalavu has assured medical students who have completed their internships and are waiting to be posted that they will be employed by next month.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 27/07/2026

Minister for Health, Doctor Ratu Atonio Lalabalavu has assured medical students who have completed their internships and are waiting to be posted that they will be employed by next month.

This follows concerns raised with fijivillage News that some medical graduates who have completed their internships are still waiting to be posted.

Dr Lalabalavu says there was a procedural issue that resulted in some medical graduates having to wait for their postings.

He says the selection and finalisation process is currently underway, and they should all be posted by August.

item.title: $1.6 million evacuation centre to recognise Viria Village's contribution to Fiji's water security
item.description: A new $1.6 million evacuation centre will soon provide the people of Viria Village in Naitasiri with a safer place during natural disasters, while recognising the community's contribution to one of Fiji's most important water infrastructure projects. Public Works , Meteorological Services and Transport Minister Ro Filipe Tuisawau officiated at the groundbreaking ceremony for the $1,604,107 Viria V
item.content:encoded:
A new $1.6 million evacuation centre will soon provide the people of Viria Village in Naitasiri with a safer place during natural disasters, while recognising the community's contribution to one of Fiji's most important water infrastructure projects.

Public Works , Meteorological Services and Transport Minister Ro Filipe Tuisawau officiated at the groundbreaking ceremony for the $1,604,107 Viria Village Evacuation Centre , say ing the project reflects the coalition government's commitment to strengthening disaster resilience while giving back to resource-owner communities that have made significant contributions to Fiji's national development.

Ro Filipe says Viria Village played a vital role in Fiji's development by allowing the construction of the new main raw water intake, a critical infrastructure project that strengthened water security for the Greater Suva Area and lower-lying communities along the corridor.

He says the evacuation centre is one way the government is recognising and rewarding the sacrifices made by the resource owners for the benefit of all Fijians.

The Minister stressed that communities contributing to nationally significant infrastructure projects should also receive meaningful and lasting development benefits.

He says the Viria project is part of a national programme to construct modern, multi-purpose evacuation centres for resource-owner communities across the country.

Viria Village joins Nagado Village in the Western Division, Nasealevu Village in Macuata in the Northern Division and Tamavua Village in the Central Division as beneficiaries under the programme.

The new double-storey facility will include a Women's Resource Centre, a fully equipped kitchen, a dispensary room, accessible washroom facilities and a spacious community hall that can be used for village meetings, training programmes, youth activities and other community events.

Construction is expected to take about 20 weeks, subject to weather and site conditions, with works continuing in the 2026-2027 financial year following the Government stand-down period.

Ro Filipe encouraged the people of Viria to take ownership of the facility once it is completed, saying it is an investment in the village's safety, resilience and future.

He says the groundbreaking marks more than the start of construction, describing it as a shared commitment to preparedness, resilience and ensuring communities that contribute to Fiji's development also benefit from meaningful Government investment.

item.title: Traditional Fijian welcome marks AIIB President Zou Jiayi's first official visit to Fiji
item.description: Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank President Zou Jiayi has reaffirmed the bank's long-term commitment to Fiji's development, saying AIIB will remain a reliable partner in building critical infrastructure and supporting the country's journey towards a modern and prosperous future. Speaking during the traditional welcoming ceremony in the Grand Pacific Hotel this morning, Zou acknowledges the Gove
item.content:encoded:
Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank President Zou Jiayi has reaffirmed the bank's long-term commitment to Fiji's development, saying AIIB will remain a reliable partner in building critical infrastructure and supporting the country's journey towards a modern and prosperous future.

Speaking during the traditional welcoming ceremony in the Grand Pacific Hotel this morning, Zou acknowledges the Government of Fiji for its warm hospitality during her first visit to the country in her capacity as President of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank.

She says she is deeply moved by the traditional Fijian welcoming ceremony.

Insert: Zou on welcoming ceremony 27th July 26

According to Zou, these are not only the values of Fiji but also those of AIIB as a multilateral development bank, as well as the principles of multilateralism.

She stresses that history and the future, as well as tradition and modernisation, should never be seen as separate, saying development can only succeed when it is rooted in a nation's history, culture and identity.

Zou says AIIB is committed to becoming part of Fiji's development agenda, noting that when she arrived at Nadi International Airport she saw a map of Fiji showing airports across many of the country's islands.

She says this highlights the critical role infrastructure plays in connecting communities and supporting Fiji's development.

The AIIB President says the bank builds infrastructure while Fiji continues to build a modern and prosperous nation, adding that both share the common goal of development.

She assures the Government of Fiji that AIIB will remain a reliable development partner as the country continues its development journey.

item.title: Former Hibiscus Queens return to support 70th Hibiscus Festival
item.description: Three former Hibiscus Queens will return as volunteers to help organise the 2026 Hibiscus Festival as the event celebrates its 70th anniversary. Festival Director Ellen Whippy-Knight confirms that Michele Smith (1975) , Patricia Naisara (2007) and Alisi Rabukawaqa (2011) have joined the organising team to support this year's festival, which will be held in Suva next month.
item.content:encoded:
Three former Hibiscus Queens will return as volunteers to help organise the 2026 Hibiscus Festival as the event celebrates its 70th anniversary.

Festival Director Ellen Whippy-Knight confirms that Michele Smith (1975) , Patricia Naisara (2007) and Alisi Rabukawaqa (2011) have joined the organising team to support this year's festival, which will be held in Suva next month.

Whippy-Knight says the three former queens are volunteering their time, skills and festival experience to support the current generation of contestants.

She says Rabukawaqa will oversee the pageant activities for this year's 12 contestants, while Naisara will serve as the Master of Ceremonies for the crowning ceremony at Albert Park on 5th September.

Whippy-Knight also says Smith, who recently returned to Fiji after many years overseas, has used her professional experience to develop a new Queens Mentoring Programme.

Smith says giving back to the community has always been important to her, and she feels privileged to support the Hibiscus Festival more than 50 years after being crowned queen.

Festival organisers are also inviting other former Hibiscus Queens to come forward and volunteer, sharing their knowledge and experience with this year's contestants.

The 2026 Hibiscus Festival will be held from August 29th to September 5th at Albert Park.

item.title: Koroipita Youth Club members is lead community clean-up
item.description: Youths of the Koroipita Youth Club in Lautoka are making a difference in their community by volunteering their time to improve the environment, assist vulnerable residents and strengthen community spirit. Club members spent yesterday morning working in the community nursery, where they prepared and fertilised the soil before planting seedlings as part of their ongoing environmental initiative.
item.content:encoded:
Youths of the Koroipita Youth Club in Lautoka are making a difference in their community by volunteering their time to improve the environment, assist vulnerable residents and strengthen community spirit.

Club members spent yesterday morning working in the community nursery, where they prepared and fertilised the soil before planting seedlings as part of their ongoing environmental initiative.

The youths also cleared a blocked drain outside the home of a single mother after soil erosion caused it to clog for several weeks, creating an unpleasant smell.

The Koroipita Youth Club says members successfully removed the blockage, making the area cleaner and safer for the family and surrounding neighbours.

President of the Koroipita Youth Club, Jotame Ratabua says the club's Dual Transformation initiative is about changing themselves while inspiring others to do the same.

Ratabua says every effort counts, and by engaging young people in community service , they are helping them channel their energy into positive actions, build confidence and become responsible leaders.

He says everything starts at home, with parents playing a vital role in raising children with strong values, respect and discipline.

Ratabua says many of the social issues Fiji faces today can be addressed by raising young people in a positive and supportive environment.

He adds that families and communities must work together to inspire the next generation to make a difference and build a stronger, safer and brighter Fiji.

After the community work, the volunteers gathered for breakfast at House 300, where parents prepared and served a meal in appreciation of their efforts.

The day concluded with friendly sports at the community sports court, giving members the opportunity to strengthen friendships, build teamwork and promote healthy lifestyles.

The Koroipita Youth Club says it is proud of its young members for their willingness to serve others, take on leadership roles and contribute positively to the community as they continue working towards building a stronger and more caring Koroipita.

item.title: Work to remove first three derelict vessels from Suva Harbour set to begin
item.description: The committee agreed to move ahead with the next phase of the clean-up under the Captain Johnathan Smith Fund, which aims to improve the condition of Suva Harbour. Permanent Secretary in the Office of the Prime Minister, Dr Lesikimacuata Korovavala, said careful planning had been undertaken to ensure the project was ready to progress.
item.content:encoded:
The committee agreed to move ahead with the next phase of the clean-up under the Captain Johnathan Smith Fund, which aims to improve the condition of Suva Harbour.

Permanent Secretary in the Office of the Prime Minister, Dr Lesikimacuata Korovavala, said careful planning had been undertaken to ensure the project was ready to progress.

He says the Captain Johnathan Smith Fund continues the legacy of the late Captain Johnathan Smith, with the goal of creating a cleaner and healthier Suva Harbour for future generations.

The meeting followed the finalisation of an operational agreement outlining how the clean-up will be managed by the Government, the Joint Maritime Environment Committee, Fiji Ports Corporation Limited, the Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji, the Waitt Institute and Blue Prosperity Fiji.

Fiji Ports Corporation Limited will oversee all operational aspects of the vessel removal, including managing contractors responsible for cleaning and scuttling the vessels in line with Fiji's legal requirements.

The vessels will only be scuttled after meeting strict environmental and safety standards certified by the Department of Environment and the Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji.

Permanent Secretary for Environment and Climate Change, Dr Sivendra Michael says removing derelict vessels from Suva Harbour demonstrates Fiji's commitment to protecting its marine environment and meeting its environmental and climate commitments.

He adds that the abandoned vessels have posed risks to traditional custodians, marine ecosystems, navigation and public safety for many years, and their removal will help restore the ecological integrity of the harbour.
